chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Shayban narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn Kulayb al-Mas'oodi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hakam ibn Sulayman narrated from Muhammad ibn Kathir, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhrami, who said:

Abban and I entered upon Abu Abdillah, and that was when the black banners had appeared in Khurasan. We said: 'What do you think?' He said: 'Stay in your houses, and when you see that we have united upon a man, then rush to us with your weapons.'

key_terms.ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ: Muhammad ibn Kathir, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.الرِّيَاطُ السُّودُ: The black banners, referring to the Abbasid revolts
key_terms.الْحَضْرَمِيِّ: Al-Hadhrami, referring to Abu Bakr from the Hadhram tribe
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: Khurasan, a historical region in Persia

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq advise his followers to do during the Abbasid revolts in Khurasan?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* captures the strategic patience of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) during the volatile pre-revolutionary period of the Abbasid uprising, emphasizing the distinction between general waiting and active participation. The Imam’s directive to remain in their homes until the 'party' (Hizb) coalesced around a single leader underscores the Shia principle of avoiding premature uprisings that lack unified command, a key theme in the doctrine of *al-intizar* (waiting for deliverance).
